text:
olivia: Heads up — customer Kestrel Health flagged invoice INV-2026-089. It contains a dedicated pool overage charge (~$12k) that doesn't match their reported failover window. Can finance pause payment capture while we reconcile?

jon: Putting a hold sounds right. Do we need legal sign-off or just an internal hold + note on the invoice?

priya: Internal hold is fine for now but we should capture reason code. I'll add HOLD:pending-recon and tag the AR record. Need the usage breakdown to confirm whether it's burst or misattributed reserved units.

olivia: Copying the key lines from the billing export (redacted):
```
customer: Kestrel Health
commit_pool_id: pool-0a1b
reserved_nodes: 8
actual_peak_nodes: 11
overage_hours: 64
metered_tokens_equiv: 9.2e6
line_total: $12,342.00
```
Note: customer claims they routed failover to DR region for 2 hours on 2026-03-05 — should have been covered by cross-region failover cushion per the SLA.

ryan: I spoke with SEs — their app did an emergency switchover but traffic stayed within the same committed capacity in eu-west. The 11-node peak looks like a telemetry spike from a migration job not covered by failover rules. Need to check if our routing policy attributed traffic to a dedicated pool vs. burst metering.

jon: Priya, can you run a reconciliation against the meter logs for pool-0a1b between 2026-03-04 22:00 UTC and 2026-03-06 04:00 UTC? If the spike is internal migration traffic flagged as user traffic, we should credit.

priya: On it. I already pulled the raw events and will diff commit tag vs metered tag. ETA 3 hours. If it's our platform routing misclassification, we propose full SLA credit + reverse the invoice line.

olivia: Customer is asking for a temporary waiver to avoid collection notices. Can we approve a short-term goodwill hold while recon runs?

jon: Approve a 14-day billing hold on the line item with note: "investigating dedicated pool overage - do not collect". I'll update billing system and block dunning.

billing-bot: Invoice INV-2026-089 status updated -> hold:true, hold_reason:"investigating dedicated pool overage - do not collect", hold_expiry: 2026-04-10

ryan: If priya confirms it's a platform attribution bug, I'll create a remediation ticket for eng-runtime with the request: "ensure failover traffic inherits reserved pool tag" and ask for a backfill for March 5th usage.

priya: Reconciled metrics attached (s3://redwood-billing-recon/kestrel/INV-2026-089.csv). Quick summary: 52 of the 64 overage hours align with internal migration job id=mig-448; remaining 12 hours are real customer traffic. Recommending a pro-rated SLA credit of 81% of the overage line -> credit ~$9,990 and reverse remaining balance.

olivia: I'll propose the credit to the customer and ask them to confirm they won't need a larger adjustment.

jon: Approving the 81% SLA credit. Finance will issue credit memo CM-2026-114 and apply to INV-2026-089. Priya please include a short audit note referencing the reconciliation file.

priya: Will do. Adding audit note and setting invoice to partial-credit. Also opening vendor ticket with eng-runtime: RTR-2026-55 to prevent recurrence.

olivia: Thanks team — logging this as "billing hold + partial SLA credit approved". I'll follow up with Kestrel after I get the confirmation message. :thumbsup:

ryan: FYI, I'll include a short runbook in the ticket so SEs know how to avoid the migration job tagging issue going forward.

jon: Closing action items: (1) billing hold applied, (2) priya to attach reconciliation and issue credit memo, (3) ryan to file eng remediation. Reopen if anything else comes up.

olivia: Closing the loop — customer acknowledged the proposed credit and withdrawal of dunning. They'll accept CM-2026-114 once posted.
